sentences.text: March, 2023  THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE V.GOPALA KRISHNA RAO  M.A.C.M.A.No.902 of 2012 JUDGEMENT:

The appellants are the Claimants in M.V.O.P.No.82 of 2009 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- XIII Additional District & Sessions Judge, Narasaraopet and the respondents are the respondents in the said case.
2. Both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in claim application.
3.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- XIII Additional District & Sessions Judge, Narasaraopet
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The claimants filed a Claim Petition under sections 140 and 163-A of Motor Vehicles Act against the respondents praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards compensation on account of death of deceased Vemula Mukkanti in a Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 22.11.2008.
4.

The case of the claimants is that on 22.11.2008 at about 9.00 a.m. at Macherla-Guntur main road,
when the deceased was standing on the left side of the road margin in front of Venkateswaramma hotel, Kambampadu village, the driver of lorry VGKRJ MACMA 902 of 2012 bearing No.AP 07 Y 3798 came from Macherla side at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased Vemula Mukkanti, resulting which, the deceased sustained fatal injuries, later succumbed to injuries and the petitioners claimed an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- towards compensation.
5.
The first respondent remained exparte.

The second respondent filed counter by denying the claim application and contended that the claimants are not entitled any compensation and the second respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.

6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i. Whether the deceased died in the accident caused due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry bearing No.AP 07 Y 3798 by its driver?
ii.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what would be the just amount of compensation that the petitioners would be entitled and against whom?

iii. To what relief?

sentences.text: On behalf of the petitioners, PW1 was examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.A7 were marked.

No oral and documentary evidence was marked on behalf of respondents.
8.

After considering the evidence on record, the Tribunal has given a finding that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle and the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.7,000/- to the claimants towards compensation.
9. Aggrieved by the same, the claimants filed the present appeal by claiming the remaining balance of compensation amount.

10. Now, the point for consideration is:
 I. Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any  interference?
 II. Whether the petitioners are entitled for enhancement  of compensation as prayed for?

11. POINT Nos.1 and 2:-
The case of the claimants is that on 22.11.2008 at about 9.00 a.m. at Macherla-Guntur main road, when the deceased was VGKRJ MACMA 902 of 2012 standing on the left side of the road margin in front of Venkateswaramma Hotel,
Kambampadu village, the driver of lorry bearing No.AP 07 Y 3798 came from Macherla side at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased Vemula Mukkanti, resulting which, the deceased received fracture injuries, after the accident he was shifted to Government Hospital, Macherla and thereafter to Government General Hospital, Guntur and he was discharged from the Government General Hospital, Guntur on 07.12.2008, later the said Vemula Mukkanti died due to injuries on 30.12.2008 at his house.
12.
In order to prove the claim of the petitioners, the petitioners relied on the evidence of PW1.
PW1 is none other than the wife of the said late Vemula Mukkanti and first petitioner in this case.
As per her evidence, she is not an eye witness to the accident.
Ex.A1 certified copy of First Information Report and Ex.A2 certified copy of charge sheet are relied by the claim petitioners.
Ex. A1

goes to show that Macherla Rural police registered a case in Crime No.56 of 2008 under Section 337 of Indian Penal code and Ex.A2 goes to show that the charge sheet was filed against the driver of the VGKRJ MACMA 902 of 2012 offending vehicle by name Upputhola Gopi on the file of Judicial Magistrate of I Class, Macherla.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of I Class, Macherla
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Ex.A3 certified copy of wound certificate shows that the deceased Vemula Mukkanti sustained injuries in the said accident.

The evidence on record i.e., Ex.A1 and Ex.A2 coupled with the evidence of PW1 clearly goes to show that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No.AP 07 Y 3798 and the first respondent is the owner of the said lorry.

The Tribunal after giving cogent reasons came to the Vemula Seethamma 5 Others vs U. Govinda Raju Another on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55252846/
2 conclusion that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: No appeal is filed by the respondents against the said finding.
Therefore, there is no need to interfere with the said finding given by the Tribunal.

13. The contention of the petitioners is that the deceased Vemula Mukkanti met with an accident on 22.11.2008 and he was admitted in the hospital on 23.11.2008, later he was discharged from Government General Hospital, Guntur on 7.12.2008 and later he died on 30.12.2008 at his house,
due to accident injuries.
Admittedly there is no evidence on record that the deceased died VGKRJ MACMA 902 of 2012 due to the said accident injuries after a lapse of 40 days of accident.

First Information Report is not registered against the driver of lorry for an offence under Section 304-A of Indian Penal code and the charge sheet was also filed against the driver of the lorry for the offence under Section 338 of Indian Penal Code only.
In the present case no inquest report and no Post Mortem Examination reports were marked as exhibits.
As per the case of the petitioners, the death was not reported to the concerned police, even though the death certificate issued by the Panchayat was filed by the petitioners and got marked as Ex.A5.
To prove the death of Vemula Mukkanti, there is no whisper in Ex.A5 about the cause of death of deceased.
No evidence is produced by the claim petitioners that the said Vemula Mukkanti died due to accident injuries after lapse of 40 days from the date of accident.
Here the legal representatives of Vemula Mukkanti filed the claim petition for the injuries sustained by the said Mukkanti in a road accident which was occurred on 22.11.2008.
By the date of filing of claim petition, the said Vemula Mukkanti was no more.

The claim has to be decided, the liability of the owner of the vehicle and insurer to pay the compensation for the injuries sustained by the deceased Vemula Mukkanti in a road accident VGKRJ MACMA 902 of 2012 does not come to an end.
Here in the present case, the claim petitioners failed to prove the said Vemula Mukkanti died at his house due to accident injuries only and his death is not a natural death.
The liability subsists when the legal representatives of the claimant i.e., injured would step into the shoes of injured.
The liability would not be towards legal representatives, on account of the accident itself.
The entitlement of legal representatives would be confined to the amount, which the injured claimant could have recovered had he been alive.

14. In the present case on hand Ex.A3 certified copy of wound certified produced by the petitioners goes to show that the deceased sustained one grievous injury and one simple injury and also he was hospitalized from 23.11.2008 to 7.12.2008 nearly at about 15 days.
The learned Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.3,000/- towards loss of earnings, Rs.3,000/- towards attendant charges and extra nourishment of food and Rs.1,000/- towards transportation charges.

In total, the learned Tribunal granted an amount of Rs,7,000/- only towards compensation to the claimants, but the learned Tribunal failed to grant compensation in respect of grievous and simple VGKRJ MACMA 902 of 2012 injuries and also pain and suffering sustained by the deceased Mukkanti.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.20,000/- is awarded towards one grievous injury and amount of Rs.2,000/- is awarded towards one simple injury.
This Court has clearly stated above that the petitioners failed to prove that because of the accident injuries, the said Vemula Mukkanti i.e., injured died at his house.
Since the deceased Vemula Mukkanti was hospitalized for a period of nearly 15 days, he is entitled an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Here the deceased Mukkanti was hospitalized for a period of 15 days, therefore, an amount of Rs.3,000/- is awarded towards medical expenses.
In total an amount of Rs.35,000/- is awarded to the claimants for the injuries sustained by the Vemula Seethamma 5 Others vs U. Govinda Raju

3 deceased Vemula Mukkanti, in addition to the amount of Rs.7,000/- awarded by the learned Tribunal.
Here, the legal representatives of the deceased Vemula Mukkanti filed the claim petition for enhancement of compensation.

Accordingly, the first petitioner, who is the wife of deceased is entitled to receive the said enhanced compensation of Rs.35,000/- from the respondents 1 and 2.
VGKRJ MACMA 902 of 2012 15.

In the result, the appeal is allowed in-part, by modifying the order dated 10.08.2010 passed in MVOP No.82/2009 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum- XIII Additional District & Sessions Judge, Narasaraopet.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is held that the first appellant is entitled to receive the enhanced compensation of Rs.35,000/- with interest @7.5% p.a., from the date of petition, till the date of payment.
The respondents 1 and 2 are directed to deposit the enhanced amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
On such deposit, the first appellant is entitled to withdraw the same along with accrued interest thereon.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
